html:
The Zulu Kingdom was a monarchy in south-eastern Africa, in what is now KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa, from about 1816 to 1897. It was built by Shaka, who turned a small Zulu chiefdom into a strong military state.

Shaka organised young men into age regiments that lived in royal barracks, drilled them to fight at close quarters with a short stabbing spear, and absorbed or broke neighbouring chiefdoms. These wars belong to a wider time of upheaval across southern Africa called the Mfecane; historians still argue over how much the Zulu caused it.

  • 1828: Shaka was killed by his half-brothers, and Dingane became king.
  • 1838: Dingane fought Boer settlers of the Great Trek and lost the Battle of Blood River.
  • 1856: a civil war between the brothers Cetshwayo and Mbuyazi ended in Cetshwayo's victory.

In 1879 Britain invaded, starting the Anglo-Zulu War. On 22 January the Zulu army destroyed a British column at the Battle of Isandlwana, one of the worst defeats of a colonial army in Africa. Britain sent more troops and won at Ulundi in July. Cetshwayo was captured and the kingdom split into thirteen chiefdoms, which soon fought each other. Britain annexed Zululand in 1887 and joined it to the colony of Natal in 1897, as part of the British Empire. The Zulu king is still recognised today.
sum: The Zulu Kingdom was a monarchy in south-eastern Africa, in what is now KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa, from about 1816 to 1897. It was built by Shaka, who turned a small Zulu chiefdom into a strong military state.
